reviewKind: independent language and policy contract review
scope: compiler-owned initial state and lifecycle field writes
ordinary and joined-row visibility before limit
UserDisabled authority resolution for hidden Users
logical transition permissions and concealed outcomes

findings.title: Purge authority conflicts with the accepted job policy boundary
evidence: docs/lifecycle-plan.md:90 and :124-129 prohibit ordinary Todo hard deletion yet give a compiler-owned privileged durable job physical deletion of hidden rows without naming its policy authority.
docs/policy-plan.md POLICY-D30 requires jobs and internal callers, including generated/scheduled ones, to obey entity policy; POLICY-D12 is default-deny.
examples/golden-todo-migration/entities/todo.jadpo currently grants TodoRole.owner only [create, read, update, delete], and examples/golden-todo/policy.jadpo has no purge principal or permission.
findings.impact: A lowering can either bypass the accepted entity-policy rule or fail closed and never purge. A privileged hidden-row exception is consequential and cannot be inferred from scheduling alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Before freeze, define a narrow, unforgeable retention-maintenance authority and checked effect for this compiler-owned operation, including who may activate it, its exact deleted-and-aged row scope, and its audit/approval facts. Reconcile explicitly with POLICY-D30 (or obtain a reviewed policy decision for a distinct compiler maintenance plane). Add compile-negative cases for an authored job/action attempting the purge or a hidden-row hard delete, plus a positive authorized maintenance case.

findings.title: Disabled-owner reminder selection lacks a direct contract case
evidence: docs/lifecycle-plan.md:95-98 says joined visibility applies before limit; examples/golden-todo/app.jadpo:528-541 selects Todo with a required owner and checks owner.status after the limited query.
examples/golden-todo/acceptance.json JOB-003 requires zero mail for a Todo whose owner is disabled.
tests/assurance/lifecycle-v0.1.json covers Todo deleted-row pagination but no disabled-owner join/reminder case.
findings.impact: The first lowering could filter disabled owners after LIMIT, shrink a reminder batch, or expose a hidden User through a required include.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a catalog case with more than 500 earlier eligible-looking Todos belonging to disabled Users followed by an active-owner Todo. Require the User visibility predicate in the authoritative joined selection before order/limit, no hidden User projection or mail, and the active-owner Todo selected; also cover direct read concealment.

reviewedWithoutFinding: The text expressly keeps policy, lifecycle, business predicates and generated ownership as separate audit facts, and maps Todo's transition to logical delete permission despite update SQL.
An owning transition requires identity-bounded authoritative conditional mutation with visibility and from guards in the same transaction; concurrent hidden-row losers return concealed missing.
The hidden-User authentication exception is restricted to compiler-owned subject/identity/lifecycle lookup and preserves fresh UserDisabled versus ordinary read concealment.
The transition clock obtains a new snapshot on a proved-safe retry, consistent with TIME-D05; no claim of one instant across attempts remains.
limits: This is a review of the candidate contract and static case catalog. No lifecycle compiler/runtime implementation or executable conformance is claimed.

originalFindings.evidence: The owner-selected retention maintenance plane is separate from POLICY-D30 application jobs, has only a checked clause-bound physical purge effect, uses a non-source-mintable internal capability, rechecks hidden/expired state in the authoritative delete transaction, limits deterministic batches to 500, preserves referential constraints, and requires explicit redacted audit. POLICY-D30-M1 records this narrow exception; cases maintenance_purge_authorized, authored_purge_job, forged_maintenance_capability, and maintenance_guard_and_audit cover positive and negative boundaries.

The contract requires Todo and required User visibility before reminder order/limit. Cases disabled_owner_before_reminder_limit and disabled_user_direct_read test 501 hidden earlier owner rows, active-owner selection, no hidden projection/mail, and ordinary concealment.

newFindings.title: The pinned approved policy digest no longer clearly identifies the amended section
evidence: docs/policy-plan.md:9 labels sha256:66e7a8f586b62ed92c3a7220f524e25aee5808ca60b8504fb3c2d225ef2d68bd the accepted-contract digest of section 2, while new POLICY-D30-M1 is now inside section 2.
docs/decision-register.md:449-452 and docs/decision-sprint.md:79-80 still describe that same digest as the pinned accepted section-2 contract.
newFindings.impact: A reviewer cannot tell whether the pinned digest denotes the original approved section or the current owner-amended policy boundary. The new maintenance authority must be traceable as a deliberate addendum rather than silently appearing under the old pin.
newFindings.suggestedFix: Preserve the original digest as the historic D01-D43 baseline, mark D30-M1 as the dated owner-approved addendum, and record exact current-section provenance in the policy and decision references (or repin through the approved decision process). Then repeat a short provenance check; the lifecycle semantics themselves need no further change for this finding.

reviewedWithoutNewFinding: No new contradiction found in hidden User authentication resolution, logical Todo delete permission, guarded transition atomicity, or TIME-D05 per-attempt clock.
The maintenance capability is internal to the compiler/host boundary and does not add an authored permission vocabulary or general source capability.
reReviews.limits: Contract and assurance-catalog review only; the 27 catalog cases are not executable lifecycle conformance evidence.

findingResolution.evidence: DATA-007 restricts retention_purge to a checked, host-started compiler maintenance capability with a same-transaction expiry/deletion guard, deterministic 500-row bound and explicit audit. POLICY-D30 continues to govern authored jobs; D30-M1 is a separately reviewed candidate addendum.
DATA-007 and the catalog require joined Todo and User visibility before reminder order/limit, with 501 disabled-owner rows, an active-owner successor and direct hidden-User read concealment.

The unchanged policy section-2 UTF-8 bytes hash exactly to the original approved digest. D30-M1 is outside that section in section 19 and its separately stated row hash matches; the decision register distinguishes historic approval from the owner-selected candidate addendum, and DATA-007 links it.

reReviews.nonblockingConsistencyNote: The earlier RM-108 work-plan prose still says to compose named Todo queries/actions with jobs including retention purge. Before implementing RM-108, update that plan so reminder work uses authored job composition while retention purge uses the clause-bound generated maintenance worker; retain the frozen app as provenance.
reReviews.limits: Approval is for the source and behavior contract only. The 27 catalog cases are not executable lifecycle conformance, and this review does not approve future compiler/runtime lowering or protected deployment.
